preconditions.description: Attacker must be the admin of the TransparentUpgradeableProxy contract

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the admin of the TransparentUpgradeableProxy, call upgradeTo() or upgradeToAndCall() to change the implementation contract to a malicious one. This allows you to execute arbitrary code through the proxy, potentially stealing funds or manipulating contract logic. The attack requires admin privileges which may be obtained through social engineering, compromised keys, or improper access control in the admin contract.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The TransparentUpgradeableProxy contract has an admin role that can upgrade the implementation contract. If an attacker gains admin privileges (through storage manipulation, compromised keys, or social engineering), they can change the implementation to a malicious contract, allowing arbitrary code execution through the proxy. The oracle checks that _getImplementation() != address(0), which will be true after we upgrade to a non-zero implementation address.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Overwrite the admin storage slot to make ourselves the admin. 2. Deploy a simple malicious implementation contract. 3. Call upgradeTo() on the proxy to change the implementation to our malicious contract. 4. Verify the implementation has changed.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Calculate the admin slot (0xb53127684a568b3173ae13b9f8a6016e243e63b6e8ee1178d6a717850b5d6103). 2. Use vm.store() to set the admin to address(this). 3. Deploy a simple contract that will serve as the new implementation. 4. Call upgradeTo() on the proxy with the new implementation address. 5. Verify _getImplementation() returns our new address.
